As far as the bloating goes, try a low FODMAP diet for a couple weeks and see if it helps. FODMAPS are certain poorly digested sugars that bacteria in your bowels will consume and release a ton of gas. If you experience relief after two weeks on the diet, reintroduce high FODMAP foods one by one to see which you can tolerate and which cause issues.

Assuming you don't have a serious problem, and in all likelihood you don't, it's my personal opinion that you need to come to terms with the fact that you can't look shredded all the time.

Secondly, getting more fiber in your diet should help with constipation. That probably means you're going to have to add the carbs back in. Carbs are not evil. They are the primary fuel source for your body, and this includes your brain. Excess carbs get stored as glycogen before fat, and the efficiency of turning carbs to fat is very poor. On the other hand, fat gets stored by the body pretty much directly as fat. This makes fat way more of an enemy than carbs.

That said, it's still a good idea to avoid simple carbs. This means refined and added sugars. Cakes, cokes, cookies, etc. Stay clear. Make sure your sugars are coming with a good load of fiber and nutrients. Eat fruits, vegetables, and whole grains. Simple carbs will spike your blood sugar whereas complex carbs won't. A spike in blood sugar causes a spike in insulin, resulting in a dramatic drop in blood sugar, making you tired and craving more sugar. It's a vicious cycle.
